verses.rationale: Adam includes any person; retains all three uncertain symptom terms and the priestly family. Defiling skin disease identifies the ritual category, not a modern diagnosis.
verses.before: “When a person has on the skin of the body a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes a diseased condition on the skin, that person will be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.
verses.after: “When someone develops a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot on their skin that becomes a sign of defiling skin disease, they must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who serves as a priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When a person has on the skin of the body a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes a diseased condition on the skin, that person shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

verses.rationale: Keeps both diagnostic observations conjunctive and separates examination from the declaration; avoids calling the condition contagious.
verses.before: The priest will examine the diseased area on the skin. If the hair in the diseased area has turned white and the appearance of the diseased area is deeper than the skin, it is a serious skin disease. The priest will examine the person and pronounce that person unclean.
verses.after: The priest must examine the affected area. If the hair there has turned white and the area looks deeper than the surrounding skin, it is defiling skin disease. After examining it, the priest must declare the person unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall examine the diseased area on the skin. If the hair in the diseased area has turned white and the appearance of the diseased area is deeper than the skin, it is a serious skin disease. The priest shall examine the person and pronounce that person unclean.

verses.rationale: Retains the negative depth and hair criteria; the affected patch stands for the person confined, without naming a modern quarantine policy.
verses.before: But if the bright spot is white on the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, and the hair has not turned white, the priest will isolate the affected person for seven days.
verses.after: If the bright spot on the skin is white but does not look deeper than the skin, and the hair has not turned white, the priest must confine the person for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the bright spot is white on the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, and the hair has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the affected person for seven days.

verses.rationale: Makes the priest the observer of amad be-enav and preserves the second seven-day interval.
verses.before: The priest will examine the person on the seventh day. If in his eyes the diseased area has stayed the same and has not spread on the skin, the priest will isolate the person for seven more days.
verses.after: On the seventh day the priest must examine it. If he sees that the affected area is unchanged and has not spread across the skin, he must confine the person for another seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall examine the person on the seventh day. If in his eyes the diseased area has stayed the same and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall isolate the person for seven more days.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the second seventh day; retains both criteria and distinguishes the priest's verdict from the person's washing.
verses.before: The priest will examine the person again on the seventh day. If the diseased area has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest will pronounce the person clean; it is a scab. The person will wash their clothes and be clean.
verses.after: At the end of that second seven-day period, the priest must examine it again. If the affected area has faded and has not spread across the skin, he must declare the person clean. It is a scab. The person must wash their clothes, and they will be clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall examine the person again on the seventh day. If the diseased area has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall pronounce the person clean; it is a scab. The person shall wash their clothes and be clean.

verses.rationale: Renders the emphatic spread construction as a contrasting condition; keeps renewed presentation after the earlier clean verdict.

verses.tsw_comparator: But if the scab spreads on the skin after the person has shown themselves to the priest for cleansing, that person shall appear again before the priest.

verses.rationale: Keeps fading distinct from disappearance and specifies the patch, not the whole item, as what is torn out.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit ish here as man and presents both person and offerings; does not silently remove the sex-specific formulation.

verses.rationale: Keeps the specified holy slaughter location, priestly entitlement and most-holy classification without identifying this place with the inner sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Retains all three right-side sites and the blood's offering source, paralleling the earlier ordination rite without adding an interpretation.

verses.rationale: Makes the priest's palm the destination and preserves left, in contrast with the right finger in the next verse.

verses.rationale: Retains finger side, palm side, seven repetitions and divine presence; does not substitute the whole right hand for a finger.

verses.after: The priest must dip his right finger into the oil in his left palm and sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the source's healing language for the house as well as its clean verdict; full XML hash retains the source's vowel annotation.
verses.before: But if the priest comes and examines it and the condition has not spread in the house after the house was replastered, the priest will pronounce the house clean, because the condition is healed.
verses.after: But if the priest comes and finds that the growth has not spread in the house after replastering, he must declare the house clean, because the affected area has healed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the priest comes and examines it and the condition has not spread in the house after the house was replastered, the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the condition is healed.

verses.rationale: Retains all materials and purification purpose; does not import the explicit live and clean adjectives from verse 4 into this shorter list.
verses.before: To cleanse the house, he will take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop.
verses.after: To purify the house, he must take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop.
verses.tsw_comparator: To cleanse the house, he shall take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop.

verses.rationale: Keeps the slaughtered bird, fresh-water source idiom and clay vessel parallel to the person's rite.
verses.before: He will slaughter one bird in an earthen vessel over fresh water.
verses.after: He must slaughter one bird over fresh water in an earthenware vessel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall slaughter one bird in an earthen vessel over fresh water.

verses.rationale: Retains the list's source order here, all dipping materials, blood and water, and seven house sprinklings.
verses.before: He will take the cedar wood, hyssop, scarlet yarn, and living bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
verses.after: He must take the cedar wood, hyssop, scarlet yarn, and live bird, dip them in the slaughtered bird's blood and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall take the cedar wood, hyssop, scarlet yarn, and living bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full repeated six-part inventory, which is not replaced with an abbreviated reference to the ritual.
verses.before: He will cleanse the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.
verses.after: He must purify the house with the bird's blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall cleanse the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.

verses.rationale: Retains the outside-city release and atonement for a house, preventing the assumption that every atonement formula names personal moral guilt.
verses.before: Then he will let the living bird go free outside the city into the open field. Thus he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.
verses.after: He must release the live bird outside the city into the open country. In this way he must make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he shall let the living bird go free outside the city into the open field. Thus he shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.

verses.rationale: Begins the complete closing inventory without forcing a sentence break at the verse boundary.
verses.before: This is the law for every serious skin disease and itch,
verses.after: These are the instructions for every case of defiling skin disease and scaly conditions,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law for every serious skin disease and itch,

verses.rationale: Maintains the human/material link through defiling and the explanatory vocabulary; retains both object classes.
verses.before: for a diseased condition in a garment or a house,
verses.after: for defiling growths in clothing and houses,
verses.tsw_comparator: for a diseased condition in a garment or a house,

verses.rationale: Retains the same three symptom terms that opened 13:2 and the continuing list structure.
verses.before: for a swelling, scab, or bright spot,
verses.after: and for swellings, scabs, and bright spots,
verses.tsw_comparator: for a swelling, scab, or bright spot,

verses.rationale: Preserves the teaching purpose and final category summary, using both contextual English terms to represent the Hebrew's single broader tsaraat category.
verses.before: to teach when something is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law concerning serious diseased conditions.
verses.after: to teach when something is unclean and when it is clean. These are the instructions for defiling disease and growths.”
verses.tsw_comparator: to teach when something is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law concerning serious diseased conditions.

verses.rationale: Preserves both recipients and carries their instruction into the address to Israel.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps ish ish as any man and renders the contextual flesh euphemism explicitly; avoids calling the discharge gonorrhea or equating it with the semen case later.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge makes him unclean.
verses.after: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When any man has a discharge from his genitals, his discharge makes him unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge makes him unclean.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned Masoretic wording, retaining both flowing and blockage; records the longer ancient reading in a note instead of importing it silently.
verses.before: This will be his uncleanness because of the discharge: whether his body continues to flow with the discharge or his body is stopped from the discharge, it is his uncleanness.
verses.after: This is his uncleanness because of the discharge: whether his body lets the discharge flow or is blocked by it, he is unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: This shall be his uncleanness because of the discharge: whether his body continues to flow with the discharge or his body is stopped from the discharge, it is his uncleanness.

verses.rationale: Preserves lying and sitting as distinct contact cases and repeats the status for both.
verses.before: Every bed on which the man with the discharge lies will be unclean, and everything on which he sits will be unclean.
verses.after: Every bed the man with the discharge lies on becomes unclean, and anything he sits on becomes unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every bed on which the man with the discharge lies shall be unclean, and everything on which he sits shall be unclean.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three requirements, preventing washing from sounding like immediate restoration.
verses.before: Whoever touches his bed will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Anyone who touches his bed must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever touches his bed shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the two different sitters while retaining clothes, bathing and evening.
verses.before: Whoever sits on anything on which the man with the discharge sat will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Anyone who sits on something the man with the discharge has sat on must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever sits on anything on which the man with the discharge sat shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Reads flesh here as the body generally rather than narrowing contact to the genitals, with the repeated washing formula intact.
verses.before: Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Anyone who touches the body of the man with the discharge must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Makes the person spat on, not the man spitting, the subject of the cleansing obligations.
verses.before: If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Keeps merkav broader than a saddle so other riding supports are not excluded by a narrow equipment choice.
verses.before: Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.
verses.after: Anything the man with the discharge rides on becomes unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides shall be unclean.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difference between touching and carrying, and does not add clothes washing to the shorter first clause.
verses.before: Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Anyone who touches anything that was under him becomes unclean until evening. Anyone who carries those things must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Makes clear whose hands are unwashed and who must bathe; does not claim rinsing the man's hands cures or ends the discharge.
verses.before: Anyone whom the man with the discharge touches without first rinsing his hands in water will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: If the man with the discharge touches anyone without first rinsing his hands in water, the person he touches must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone whom the man with the discharge touches without first rinsing his hands in water shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Retains the material-dependent difference between destruction and rinsing; no rationale about porosity is invented.
verses.before: An earthen vessel touched by the man with the discharge will be broken, and every wooden vessel will be rinsed in water.
verses.after: An earthenware vessel touched by the man with the discharge must be broken. Any wooden utensil he touches must be rinsed in water.
verses.tsw_comparator: An earthen vessel touched by the man with the discharge shall be broken, and every wooden vessel shall be rinsed in water.

verses.rationale: Makes cessation distinct from completed ritual cleanness and preserves the special living-water requirement and seven days.
verses.before: When the man with a discharge is cleansed from his discharge, he will count seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in fresh water; then he will be clean.
verses.after: When the man is free of his discharge, he must count seven days for his cleansing. He must wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh water. Then he will be clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the man with a discharge is cleansed from his discharge, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in fresh water; then he shall be clean.

verses.rationale: Keeps two paired bird options, eighth-day timing, the man's coming and handing over rather than prematurely making the priest the initial actor.
verses.before: On the eighth day he will take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and give them to the priest.
verses.after: On the eighth day he must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and give the birds to the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and give them to the priest.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct offering roles and discharge as the stated occasion for atonement; does not add a sin or a forgiveness formula.
verses.before: The priest will offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest will make atonement for him before the LORD concerning his discharge.
verses.after: The priest must offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. He must make atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD concerning his discharge.

verses.rationale: Names semen plainly, retains whole-body washing and evening, and treats this as a separate case from the earlier discharge.
verses.before: If a man has an emission of semen, he will bathe his entire body in water and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body in water, and he remains unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his entire body in water and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Retains both materials, washing and delayed cleanness rather than adding destruction or an offering.
verses.before: Every garment and every leather article on which semen comes will be washed with water and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Any clothing or leather with semen on it must be washed in water, and it remains unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every garment and every leather article on which semen comes shall be washed with water and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sexual relation, emission and plural bathing/status requirements without adding marital status or moral disapproval.
verses.before: If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both will bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: When a man has intercourse with a woman and emits semen, both must bathe in water, and both remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Preserves the woman's seven-day interval and the contact person's evening interval as different durations; no exile rule is added.
verses.before: When a woman has a discharge, and the discharge from her body is blood, she will be in her menstrual uncleanness seven days. Whoever touches her will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: When a woman has a flow of blood from her body, she remains in her menstrual impurity for seven days. Anyone who touches her becomes unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: When a woman has a discharge, and the discharge from her body is blood, she shall be in her menstrual uncleanness seven days. Whoever touches her shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Keeps both contact surfaces and the repeated verdict parallel to the man's discharge rule.
verses.before: Everything on which she lies during her menstrual uncleanness will be unclean, and everything on which she sits will be unclean.
verses.after: Anything she lies on during her menstrual impurity becomes unclean, and anything she sits on becomes unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everything on which she lies during her menstrual uncleanness shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.

verses.rationale: Retains the three-part contact response in full for the bed.
verses.before: Whoever touches her bed will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Anyone who touches her bed must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever touches her bed shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Keeps contact with a seat distinct from contact with bedding and repeats the complete response.
verses.before: Whoever touches anything on which she sat will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Anyone who touches something she sits on must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever touches anything on which she sat shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Takes ambiguous hu as an object lying on the bed or seat; the alternative that it resumes the bed or seat itself is noted rather than concealed.
verses.before: Whether it is on the bed or on anything on which she sat, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: If something is on her bed or on what she sits on, anyone who touches it becomes unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whether it is on the bed or on anything on which she sat, whoever touches it shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Preserves intercourse, transferred impurity, seven days and bedding consequences; does not harmonize this case with later prohibitions by inventing accidental onset.
verses.before: If a man lies with her and her menstrual flow comes upon him, he will be unclean seven days, and every bed on which he lies will be unclean.
verses.after: If a man has intercourse with her and her menstrual impurity comes upon him, he becomes unclean for seven days. Every bed he lies on becomes unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man lies with her and her menstrual flow comes upon him, he shall be unclean seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

verses.rationale: Preserves both prolonged bleeding outside the usual time and bleeding extending beyond it, without assigning a cause.
verses.before: If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual period, or if the discharge continues beyond her period, all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness will be like the days of her menstrual uncleanness; she is unclean.
verses.after: If a woman bleeds for many days outside the time of her menstrual period, or her bleeding continues beyond her period, she remains unclean throughout the discharge, just as during her menstrual impurity.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual period, or if the discharge continues beyond her period, all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness shall be like the days of her menstrual uncleanness; she is unclean.

verses.rationale: Retains the extended duration and repeated comparison for both beds and seats.
verses.before: Every bed on which she lies during all the days of her discharge will be to her like the bed of her menstrual period, and everything on which she sits will be unclean like the uncleanness of her menstrual period.
verses.after: Every bed she lies on while the discharge lasts is unclean for her, just as her bed is during her menstrual impurity. Anything she sits on is also unclean, just as during her menstrual impurity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every bed on which she lies during all the days of her discharge shall be to her like the bed of her menstrual period, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean like the uncleanness of her menstrual period.

verses.rationale: Resolves plural them to the previous bed and seat and preserves both the status statement and the subsequent requirements.
verses.before: Whoever touches these things will be unclean and will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Anyone who touches these things becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever touches these things shall be unclean and shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes cessation from the following count and clean result; does not import an unstated bathing requirement from the male rule.
verses.before: But if she is cleansed from her discharge, she will count seven days, and afterward she will be clean.
verses.after: When she is free of her discharge, she must count seven days. After that she will be clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if she is cleansed from her discharge, she shall count seven days, and afterward she shall be clean.

verses.rationale: Preserves eighth-day timing, paired bird alternatives and presentation by the woman herself.
verses.before: On the eighth day she will take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: On the eighth day she must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps both offering roles and the source's discharge-impurity relation without adding personal wrongdoing or forgiveness.
verses.before: The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD concerning the uncleanness of her discharge.
verses.after: The priest must offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. He must make atonement for her before the LORD because of her unclean discharge.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement for her before the LORD concerning the uncleanness of her discharge.

verses.rationale: Preserves the address to the two leaders, death warning and divine dwelling among the people; does not add an unspecified physical separation policy.
verses.before: Thus you will keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling my tabernacle that is in their midst.
verses.after: You must keep the Israelites separate from their impurity, so they do not die in their impurity by defiling my tabernacle, which is among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you shall keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling my tabernacle that is in their midst.

verses.rationale: Retains the two distinct male conditions in the summary and continues the list into verse 33.
verses.before: This is the law concerning the man who has a discharge, and the man who has an emission of semen and becomes unclean by it,
verses.after: These are the instructions for a man with a discharge, for a man who emits semen and becomes unclean by it,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law concerning the man who has a discharge, and the man who has an emission of semen and becomes unclean by it,

verses.rationale: Keeps menstruation, both sexes with discharges and the intercourse case; menstrual wording renders the contextual davah without making a modern illness diagnosis.
verses.before: and concerning the woman during her menstrual uncleanness, and anyone, male or female, who has a discharge, and the man who lies with a woman who is unclean.
verses.after: for a woman during her menstrual impurity, for anyone with a discharge, male or female, and for a man who has intercourse with an unclean woman.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and concerning the woman during her menstrual uncleanness, and anyone, male or female, who has a discharge, and the man who lies with a woman who is unclean.
